claims.text: CSI is the standard interface through which storage systems plug into Kubernetes; a vendor's CSI driver is developed outside Kubernetes and installed into a cluster as an extension, so a new storage system needs no change to Kubernetes' code. Each driver lists the releases it supports.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Storage > Volumes > Out-of-tree volume plugins / csi (compatibility note)

claims.text: A CSI driver usually runs as Pods in the cluster: a controller part that serves the whole cluster and creates and deletes volumes in the storage system, and a node part on each node where Pods may use its volumes.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Volumes > csi (Windows CSI proxy paragraph); Volume Health Monitoring (CSI controller/node plugin)

claims.text: With a CSI driver as a StorageClass's provisioner, the controller part creates the volume and a PersistentVolume bound to the claim, at claim time or, if the class waits for the first Pod and the driver supports it, then; with reclaim policy Delete it deletes the volume.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Storage Classes > Provisioner, Volume binding mode (WaitForFirstConsumer, CSI); Persistent Volumes > Reclaiming > Delete

claims.text: When a Pod using a CSI volume is placed on a node, the kubelet there calls the driver's node part, which mounts the volume on that node and makes it available inside the Pod's containers.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Volumes > csi (NodeStageVolume/NodePublishVolume); CSIDriver API attachRequired

claims.text: A StorageClass's provisioner field names what creates its volumes; for a CSI driver it is the driver's name, but it may also name a non-CSI provisioner.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Storage > Storage Classes > Provisioner

claims.text: kind's default StorageClass standard uses the provisioner rancher.io/local-path, which runs as one local-path-provisioner Pod in namespace local-path-storage and creates folders on nodes; it is not a CSI driver.
claims.source_hint: capture outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/csi.txt; github.com/rancher/local-path-provisioner README; kind docs (default StorageClass)

claims.text: A CSI driver usually describes itself with a cluster-wide CSIDriver object named with the driver's name, the name a StorageClass gives in provisioner; kubectl get csidrivers lists these, and on donhang it prints 'No resources found': no driver here has created one.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Reference > CSIDriver v1 (metadata.name = driver name); Storage Classes > Provisioner; capture csi.txt

claims.text: Volume snapshots are supported only for CSI drivers that implement them, and need extra snapshot pieces (CRDs and a snapshot controller) installed in the cluster alongside Kubernetes; a new claim can name a VolumeSnapshot as its dataSource.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Storage > Volume Snapshots (Introduction; Provisioning Volumes from Snapshots)

claims.text: With many drivers a volume snapshot is kept by the same storage system as its volume; then losing that storage system loses the snapshots too, so a snapshot does not replace a backup copied somewhere else.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Volume Snapshots (snapshot on a storage system); where the copy lives is driver-specific (e.g. Longhorn concepts)

claims.text: A claim with no storageClassName gets the default StorageClass (standard in kind); a claim can ask for another class by naming it in storageClassName.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Persistent Volumes > Class; Storage Classes > Default StorageClass

claims.text: On staging, the db StatefulSet keeps PostgreSQL's data on a claim from kind's standard class; db-backup.sh copies the dumps to backups/staging/.
claims.source_hint: don-hang stage-3 deploy/gitops/config-repo-kustomize/base/db.yaml (StatefulSet volumeClaimTemplates); lessons k8s.l2.staging-keeps-its-data, k8s.l2.scheduled-backups

claims.text: csi.sh runs against donhang, the kind cluster of this module with one control-plane node and two workers; show prints a command before running it; the last command is printed with echo and run with 2>&1 so its message is captured.
claims.source_hint: don-hang stage-3 scripts/lib/network-lessons.sh (kubectl --context kind-donhang, show); scripts/k8s/csi.sh L18-20

claims.text: The replicated storage system of the next lesson installs its own CSI driver and a StorageClass whose provisioner names it.

A storage vendor's CSI driver is usually installed by applying manifests or a chart to a running cluster, as long as the cluster's Kubernetes release is one the driver supports; the Kubernetes code itself is not changed.
